samples.summary: Point-of-use clamp missing at the table-cell copy of the exact geometry sink the change hardened in the body layout
samples.evidence: The change normalizes the body list indent (`layout.ts:497`, `LIST_INDENT_PX * (normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel) + 1)`) with the rationale "a poisoned level multiplied into the indent is a NaN/Infinity marginLeft that blanks the block". The byte-identical expression for list items *inside table cells* is left raw: `table-layout.ts:93` computes `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` and folds it into `marginLeft` (line 101), from which `layoutBlock`/`applyAlignment`/row heights derive the whole table's and therefore the page's geometry. The same is true of every remaining raw reader: `doc-canvas.ts:599`, `paint-layout.ts:198`, `table-renderer.ts:524`, `peer-cursor.ts:254` and `:392`. Vector: any `listLevel` that is non-finite or far out of band and reaches a Block without passing `treeNodeToBlock`/`YorkieDocStore.treeNodeToBlock` (the two boundaries this change clamps) yields NaN or ~1e9-px geometry for every reader of that document, i.e. the same "blank the rendered document for every other reader" impact the change exists to prevent. I could not complete the chain to a concrete unclamped entry point for the docs *table* path — the CRDT boundaries (crdt-tree.ts:249, yorkie-doc-store.ts:501), the clipboard parser (clipboard.ts:348-351, finite-checked + clamped) and the backend read (`readDocsRoot` → docs `crdt-tree`) all clamp now — so confidence is low; the finding is that the defense now *reads* as complete (`docs/design/docs/docs.md`: "The raw readers clamp again at the point of use"; `list-level.ts:39-40`: "the raw readers call normalizeListLevel at the point of use") while five of them do not, which is the state in which the next non-CRDT entry point becomes exploitable silently.

grep listLevel across packages/frontend/src and packages/backend/src
read crdt-tree.ts treeNodeToBlock/treeNodeToCell (cell blocks do route through the clamped reader)
grep computeListCounters call sites (top-level blocks only; cell counters use Maps)
read cli/src/docs/content.ts + commands/docs.ts (Document comes from GET /content, which is served through readDocsRoot)

samples.summary: `PUT /content` ingest never validates `listLevel`, so the documented model invariant is enforced only on read
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` (line 429) validates `id`, `type`, `style` (alignment, `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` finite-checked, authored-spacing booleans) and table shape, but never `listLevel` (nor `listKind`/`headingLevel`) — `grep -i level` over the controller returns only unrelated comments. `writeDocsRoot`/`buildBlockNode` then persists it verbatim (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178`, `attrs.listLevel = String(block.listLevel)`). So an API-key holder with write scope can permanently store `listLevel: 1e9` / `"NaN"` / `{}` in the CRDT that every collaborator attaches to. The new read-side clamps neutralize today's docs readers, but the design note this change adds asserts the band as "an invariant of the model" — it is not, it is an invariant of two readers. Anything else that consumes the stored value raw (an older client without the clamp still in a browser tab, the slides tree reader, an external consumer of `GET /content`) sees the poisoned number. Clamping in `assertValidBlock` (reject or normalize to `[0, MAX_LIST_LEVEL]`) would make the ingest boundary agree with the read boundary.
searchedFor: grep listLevel in packages/backend/src (only docs-tree.ts:178 write + seed)

samples.summary: Attacker-supplied PPTX `<a:pPr lvl>` enters the shared block model unclamped, and the slides tree readers were not given the new boundary clamp
samples.evidence: `const level = pPr ? (attrInt(pPr, 'lvl') ?? 0) : 0;` (line 314) is assigned straight to `block.listLevel` (line 268) from an uploaded .pptx — `ST_TextIndentLevelType` is `[0,8]`, but nothing enforces that on import (the exporter does clamp, `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:82-86`). Slides/board text bodies render through the docs package's shared sinks, so before this change a poisoned level could reach `computeListCounters` (`paint-layout.ts:133`) — the `RangeError` the change fixes. This change clamps the docs CRDT boundaries only; the slides boundary (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts`, the frontend slides store) still admits the value, and the residual raw sink `paint-layout.ts:198` now paints the bullet at the *unclamped* x while `computeLayout` indents the text at the clamped level — layout and marker disagree for out-of-band levels where previously they at least agreed. Impact is confined to misrender of the offending text box, hence minor, but the entry point is a file upload, i.e. attacker-controlled without any collaboration privilege.
searchedFor: grep computeListCounters call sites (paint-layout.ts:133 is the slides/board paint path)

finding.summary: Peer-supplied `listLevel` is still read through a bare `Number(...)` with no clamp; the new `levelOf()` normalizer only protects the planner, so a poisoned level keeps reaching raw sinks (unbounded `String.repeat` in the markdown serializer, NaN/huge geometry in layout and PDF)
finding.evidence: The new module documents the threat itself (`packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:19-27`: "a peer's Tree attribute is read straight through `Number(...)`") and claims "Normalizing at the single point of read is what keeps both guards total". That is only true inside `planListLevelChanges`. The actual read boundaries are unchanged and unclamped: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` (`block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)`) and `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243` (same line, used for revision previews). Attack: a principal with write access to a shared doc (collaborator, or an API key with write scope via `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/content`, which does not validate `listLevel` — see the companion finding) stores `listLevel: 1e9` (or `1e400` → `"Infinity"`). Every other reader then deserializes it verbatim. Sinks reached with the raw value: `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:140` `'  '.repeat(Math.max(0, block.listLevel ?? 0))` → 2e9-char allocation or `RangeError: Invalid string length`, crashing `wafflebase docs content get --format md` (`packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129`) for anyone who exports the document; `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:494` `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` → NaN/Infinity `marginLeft` that collapses or blanks the rendered document; `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:377` → NaN/huge coordinates into pdf-lib. Note the adjacent `headingLevel` is clamped at its sink (`markdown.ts:156 clampHeadingLevel`) while `listLevel` is not. This is a persistent, other-user-affecting availability/data-integrity issue, not merely a local render glitch.

verdict.reason: The finding's central presence claim is false in this working tree. Both asserted read boundaries clamp: yorkie-doc-store.ts:501 is `block.listLevel = normalizeListLevel(Number(attrs.listLevel))` (import at :50, boundary comment :496-500), and crdt-tree.ts:250 is identical (import :40). All three sinks the finding says receive the raw value are also normalized: markdown.ts:145 uses `'  '.repeat(normalizeListLevel(block.listLevel))` rather than the quoted `Math.max(0, ...)`; layout.ts:497 and :1097 use normalizeListLevel; pdf-painter.ts:370 and :593 use normalizeListLevel. The normalizer at list-level.ts:42-46 is total (non-finite -> 0, then clamped to [0, MAX_LIST_LEVEL] via Math.floor/min/max), so the claimed attack values 1e9 and Infinity become 8 and 0; tests at test/model/list-level.test.ts:184-195 assert exactly that. It is exported from both package entries (index.ts:94, node.ts:131), so the CLI/node markdown export path gets the same clamp. Raw `block.listLevel ?? 0` reads do survive in other on-screen files (table-layout.ts:93, doc-canvas.ts:599, paint-layout.ts:198, peer-cursor.ts:254/392, table-renderer.ts:524), but those are distinct locations tracked as a separate finding and do not make this finding's asserted claim true.
